name: Naaman
overview: Naaman was a male military leader serving as the captain of the army of the king of Aram, a position of significant authority and responsibility. Scripture identifies him primarily by this role, without specifying tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His prominence in the biblical narrative is tied to his military status under King Ben-hadad.
namesAndTitles: The name Naaman means 'pleasantness' in the original language, reflecting a proper name used in the biblical text. This meaning is noted but not explicitly connected to his character or story in Scripture.
familyAndRelationships: The Bible records that Naaman was the army captain under King Ben-hadad of Aram, establishing a direct relationship of military service. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further information about his family or other personal relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Naaman's significance in the biblical account centers on his role as a leading military figure under the Aramean king, highlighting his importance in the geopolitical context of the narrative. His position as captain underscores themes of authority and service within a foreign nation, setting the stage for his interaction with God's prophet and the unfolding of divine power. This role provides a backdrop for demonstrating God's grace and sovereignty beyond Israel.
